# Sprezzature — full-text corpus

> Concatenated plain text of every English page, for single-request ingestion by an LLM/agent. French pages are translations of the same content (see llms.txt) and are not duplicated here.

# Accessibility — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/accessibility.html

sprezzature-accessibility

# Accessibility

Two halves of one job: audit what a page gets wrong about accessibility — twenty rules decidable from the HyperText Markup Language (HTML) source alone, no browser, no runtime Document Object Model (DOM, the live tree of elements a browser builds from the page) — and make the content it is missing, drafting alt text with a local vision model.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

Alt text for an image, drafted by a local Ollama vision model along the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C, the body that writes the rules of the web) image-purpose decision tree — informative, decorative, functional, text, complex, group — in any language, cached on disk

JavaScript Object Notation (JSON, a text format in which programs store data as named fields) / stdout / exit codes for pre-commit and continuous integration (CI, the server that re-runs a project's checks on every change and turns red when one fails)

An opt-in "comfortable reading" CSS (Cascading Style Sheets, the rules that give a web page its colours, fonts and spacing) toggle at the WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international rulebook that says, for example, how dark text must be against its background) 1.4.12 Text Spacing minimums, for pages that ship it as a reader-facing setting

## Audits

Missing alt, unlabelled inputs, button-without-text, clickable div

Missing dialog close, lang attribute, heading order

Color-only state, motion-reduce guards, tight letter-spacing on running text

Captions, track language and media controls on <video> and <audio>

A fast, deterministic gate (twenty rules, six with a mechanical fixer), not a replacement for axe-core / Pa11y / Lighthouse

## Say one of these

The skill triggers itself on phrasing like this, no command to memorize.

a11y lint
check this HTML for accessibility
static a11y check
WCAG-friendly lint
missing alt
unlabelled input
ARIA / keyboard check
fix accessibility

## Reference library

The knowledge the skill draws on: read them straight from the repo.

The twenty rules

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-accessibility?

Run pip install sprezzature-accessibility (Python 3.10 to 3.13): one line installs the linter, the alt-text drafter, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), and the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server, with no extras to choose. To use it as an agent skill, pip install sprezzature then sprezzature-skills --install (or sprezzature-skills --install --agent opencode ).

### What does sprezzature-accessibility check?

sprezzature-accessibility applies twenty rules decidable from the HTML source alone: missing alt text, unlabelled inputs, empty links and buttons, clickable div elements with no keyboard access, dialogs with no close, a missing lang , skipped heading levels, status shown by colour alone, animation with no reduced-motion guard, tight letter-spacing, and missing captions, transcripts or controls on video and audio. Six of the rules also have a mechanical repair, applied with --fix .

### How is sprezzature-accessibility different from axe-core, Pa11y or Lighthouse?

sprezzature-accessibility reads the HTML source without opening a browser, so it runs in milliseconds and gives the same answer every time, but it cannot see what only exists once a page renders: focus order, screen-reader timing, contrast against a real background. axe-core, Pa11y and Lighthouse drive a real browser and catch that layer; use this one as the fast first gate and one of them as the second pass, not as a replacement.

### Can sprezzature-accessibility write the missing alt text?

Yes: sprezzature-accessibility drafts the missing alt text with sprezzature-accessibility-lint --fix-alt public/ , from each image and the text around it on the same page, in the page's language or the one set by --alt-lang ; sprezzature-accessibility-alt photo.jpg does a single image. This half needs Ollama and the qwen3-vl:8b vision model, set up by sprezzature-accessibility-install-alt , while the linter needs no browser and no model. Each draft should be read by a person before it is committed.

### Does sprezzature-accessibility send my pages or images to a cloud service?

No: sprezzature-accessibility's linter keeps everything on your machine and calls no model at all; only the alt-text drafter ( --fix-alt , sprezzature-accessibility-alt ) calls a vision model, served by Ollama on your own machine unless you point OLLAMA_URL elsewhere. The HTTP API lints a string of HTML and never fetches a URL.

### Can I run sprezzature-accessibility in CI or a pre-commit hook?

Yes: sprezzature-accessibility-lint public/ lints every .html file under the folder and exits 1 on any finding, warnings included, and 0 on a clean run, with --format json for a CI parser and --ignore to skip named rules. For a hook, pip install --no-deps sprezzature-accessibility plus pip install click is enough to run the lint.

### Can I use sprezzature-accessibility without Claude Code?

Yes: sprezzature-accessibility is a Python library ( import sprezzature_accessibility ), a command line ( sprezzature-accessibility , one command per tool), an HTTP API with a Docker image, and an MCP server, sprezzature-accessibility-mcp , for any MCP client. The Docker image runs that server, so one port answers both the HTTP routes and /mcp .

### Is sprezzature-accessibility free?

Yes: sprezzature-accessibility is open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account, API key or paid tier, and the source is on GitHub .

---

# Audio — captions — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/audio.html

sprezzature-audio

# Audio: captions

Local artificial intelligence (AI) captions, speaker diarization and speaker identification for video / audio. WebVTT / SubRip subtitle format (SRT, the plain-text subtitle file most video players read) from a local whisper.cpp, who-spoke-when via NeMo, who-is-who via embeddings or a transcript pass. The audio never leaves the machine.

Work in progress: the caption backend is still settling and accuracy baselines are being collected, so captions are drafts to review.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

World Wide Web Consortium (W3C, the body that writes the rules of the web) WebVTT / SRT / plain-text captions from a local whisper.cpp build

"Who spoke when" via NVIDIA NeMo Sortformer diarization

"Who is who" via TitaNet embeddings or a transcript-mined pass

Speaker-labelled WebVTT caption format (VTT, Web Video Text Tracks, the subtitle file a web page's video player reads) with named voice cues; bilingual default, English and French

The same modality read backwards: a narration from text, landing as a WAV (Waveform Audio File Format, uncompressed sound, the file a voice recorder saves) and a WebVTT off one timeline, so a page can follow the reading sentence by sentence

Translated subtitles, through a local model

## Audits

Reading speed, line width, cue duration and overlap, against the thresholds Netflix publishes: 17 characters a second, 42 to a line, 5/6 s at the shortest, 7 s at the longest, two lines at most

Flags rather than laws, because a children’s programme and a dense talk justify different numbers

Project-vocab biasing on the caption path

## Say one of these

## Reference library

The knowledge the skill draws on: read them straight from the repo.

Captions with AI
Diarization

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-audio?

Run pip install sprezzature-audio (Python 3.10 to 3.13): captions, diarization, speaker identification, translation, narration, an API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page) and an MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server all come with it, with no extra to choose. The install includes torch, but import sprezzature_audio loads no model until a model-backed function is called.

### What does sprezzature-audio need besides pip?

sprezzature-audio needs ffmpeg and espeak-ng (for the Kokoro voice) on the system, plus model weights fetched on first use or ahead of time with sprezzature-audio-install (Whisper), sprezzature-audio-install-diarize --no-install (NeMo Sortformer and TitaNet) and sprezzature-audio-install-voice (the voices). Translation and the optional name-guessing pass also need an Ollama server serving qwen3-vl:8b . The caption audit, the speaker merge and the WER (word error rate, the share of words a transcript gets wrong) and DER (diarization error rate, the share of speaking time credited to the wrong speaker) metrics need none of this.

### Does sprezzature-audio send my audio to a cloud service?

No: sprezzature-audio transcribes with whisper.cpp, finds and names speakers with NeMo models and synthesises voices on your own machine, with no API key. Translation and name guessing call the Ollama server named by --url , on localhost by default, and the only downloads are the model weights.

### Which voices and languages does sprezzature-audio support?

sprezzature-audio narrates with three engines from speaker-helper: Kokoro (54 built-in voices, in English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Mandarin), Chatterbox, and OpenVoice, which clones a voice from a short sample. With no --voice , the language is detected from the text and a voice that speaks it is picked; a page narrated by sprezzature-publish gets the engine speaker-helper's router chooses, Chatterbox for an offline run. Captions cover the languages Whisper recognises, detected when --lang is empty.

### Can I use sprezzature-audio without Claude Code?

Yes: sprezzature-audio is also a Python library, fifteen commands behind the front door sprezzature-audio , an HTTP API with a Docker image, and an MCP server, sprezzature-audio-mcp , serving the API and /mcp on one port. The API and MCP tools cover the fast, model-free half (caption conversion, speaker merge, WER, DER); transcription and narration run as commands. The skill itself comes from pip install sprezzature then sprezzature-skills --install .

### How is sprezzature-audio different from the Whisper API, pyannote or ElevenLabs?

sprezzature-audio runs locally and works both ways, speech to timed text and text to timed speech, each landing beside a WebVTT, and it then audits the caption track for reading speed, width, duration and overlap. Hosted services such as ElevenLabs or the OpenAI audio API bill per use and receive your audio; pyannote has no ceiling on the number of speakers, whereas the Sortformer checkpoint used here is built for up to four.

### Can I run sprezzature-audio in CI?

Yes: sprezzature-audio-audit talk.vtt checks a caption track against the Netflix Timed Text Style Guide defaults (17 characters a second, 42 a line, two lines), needs only the Python standard library, prints JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, a text format in which programs store data as named fields, like {"name": "Ada"}) with --format json and exits 1 on any finding. Transcription, diarization and narration also run headless, but they download large model weights, so a CI job usually audits tracks rather than producing them.

### Is sprezzature-audio free?

Yes: sprezzature-audio is open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account, API key or paid tier, and its source is on GitHub . The models it runs are open weights downloaded to your machine, each under its own licence.

# CLI → GUI — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/cli.html

sprezzature-cli-gui

# command-line interface (CLI) → graphical user interface (GUI)

Wrap an existing command-line tool in a single-page vanilla-JavaScript (JS) + Tailwind GUI: read the arg parser, emit forms and file inputs, and build the exact command line.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

One self-contained HTML file wrapping your CLI: the markup, the Tailwind config and the script that builds the command line, all inline

Sub-commands and flags mapped to forms, segmented controls, file inputs

The exact command line, assembled in the visitor’s own browser and never run there. Copy it, or wire it to a Tauri invoke , a FastAPI endpoint, a shell

For a bespoke wrapper the agent spec goes further than the one command: host wiring, and a streaming log panel for the commands that take a while

Imports and walks the parser object itself for argparse, Click and Typer — a Typer app is converted by typer and then walked as Click, because that is what it already is

For clap, commander and cobra: --from-help runs the tool’s own --help and reads the text. Works on any CLI at all, and lower fidelity, because help text says less than a parser knows

A Click group takes its name from the decorated function, which is almost never the command you installed. Unasked, the page would build a command line that does not exist

## Audits

sprezzature-cli-gui-audit reads the parser and the page back together: every sub-command and flag reachable, no field building an option the parser rejects, no choice quietly dropped, and a command line seeded with the name the tool is installed as. Exit 1 on any finding, so it gates a build

Follows the sprezzature-ui stack rules: install sprezzature-ui alongside for the full design tokens

Hardening guidance for shipping the wrapper safely

## Say one of these

The skill triggers itself on phrasing like this, no command to memorize.

wrap this CLI in a GUI
argparse to GUI
click to web UI
GUI for my Python script
Typer / clap / cobra to GUI
frontend for a CLI
streaming log panel

## Reference library

The knowledge the skill draws on: read them straight from the repo.

Hardening

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-cli-gui?

Run pip install sprezzature-cli-gui (Python 3.10 or newer): one install brings the argparse, Click and Typer readers, the --from-help reader, the audit, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), and the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server, with no extras to choose. For the agent skill, pip install sprezzature then sprezzature-skills --install , or sprezzature-skills --install --agent opencode for OpenCode.

### Which command-line parsers can sprezzature-cli-gui read?

sprezzature-cli-gui imports and walks argparse, Click and Typer parsers directly, so every sub-command, flag and choice comes from the parser itself. A tool written in anything else, such as Go's cobra or Rust's clap, goes through --from-help , which runs the tool's own --help and reads the text, at lower fidelity.

### What does the GUI made by sprezzature-cli-gui contain?

sprezzature-cli-gui writes one self-contained HTML page in plain JavaScript and Tailwind: a collapsible section per sub-command and a field per option (checkbox, dropdown, number or text). Pressing “Build command” assembles the exact command line in the browser; the page never runs it, so you copy it or wire it to a Tauri invoke or a server.

### Does sprezzature-cli-gui send my code to a cloud service or need an AI model?

No: sprezzature-cli-gui uses no model and no Ollama, and its command line imports your CLI on your own machine; the HTTP API and the MCP server only accept the parser tree, never a module to import. The one network call is the generated page's: it loads Tailwind from cdn.tailwindcss.com for styling, and its fields still work unstyled offline.

### Can I use sprezzature-cli-gui without Claude Code?

Yes: sprezzature-cli-gui is a Python library ( walk , render_html , audit ), a command line such as sprezzature-cli-gui my_pkg.cli:build_parser --out gui.html , an HTTP API with a Docker image, and an MCP server, sprezzature-cli-gui-mcp , for any MCP client. The agent skill is only one of those ways in.

### How is sprezzature-cli-gui different from Gooey, Streamlit or Gradio?

Gooey also reads your parser, but it runs the command in a wxPython desktop window, whereas sprezzature-cli-gui emits a static HTML file that builds the command line and runs nothing. Streamlit and Gradio read no parser at all: you write every widget yourself, which is the right trade when the interface is the product rather than a face on an existing command.

### Can I run sprezzature-cli-gui in CI?

Yes: sprezzature-cli-gui-audit mytool.cli:build_parser gui.html reads the parser and the page back together and exits 1 when the page has fallen behind the CLI, for instance a flag with no field, a field for an option the parser rejects, a dropped choice or the wrong program name. Add --format json for a machine-readable report.

### Is sprezzature-cli-gui free?

Yes. sprezzature-cli-gui is open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account, API key or paid tier, and its source is on GitHub .

# Colors — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/colors.html

sprezzature-colors

# Colors

Color tooling, make and audit: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international rulebook that says, for example, how dark text must be against its background) contrast, with fixes in OKLCH (OK Lightness, Chroma, Hue, a colour space where equal steps in the numbers look like equal steps to the eye), colour-vision-deficiency (CVD, colour blindness, as in the one man in twelve who confuses red and green) simulation, a curated palette, and a Tailwind config emitter. Deterministic: no model, no network.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

A curated palette comma-separated values (CSV, a table saved as plain text, one row per line — what a spreadsheet exports) file with semantic projections

A Tailwind theme.extend.colors config from the canonical palette

Perceptual lighten / darken on the OKLCH L axis

## Audits

WCAG contrast audit with OKLCH-neighbour fix suggestions

Protanopia / deuteranopia / tritanopia simulation on screenshots

## Say one of these

The skill triggers itself on phrasing like this, no command to memorize.

is my palette accessible
colorblind preview
deuteranope / CVD
lighten this color
OKLCH
brand colors
palette to tailwind
color-blind safe

## Reference library

The knowledge the skill draws on: read them straight from the repo.

Contrast audit
CVD simulation
The palette CSV

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-colors?

Run pip install sprezzature-colors (Python 3.10 or later): one line installs the four tools, the command line, the image simulation, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), and the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server, with no extras to choose. To use it as an agent skill, pip install sprezzature then sprezzature-skills --install (or sprezzature-skills --install --agent opencode ).

### What does sprezzature-colors do?

sprezzature-colors has four tools: a WCAG contrast audit of a palette that suggests a passing colour for each failing pair, a simulation of how an image looks with protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia (plus a grayscale version), a remap of the palette to one of six accessibility levels, and an export of the palette as a Tailwind configuration. The front door is sprezzature-colors , and each tool is also its own command, such as sprezzature-colors-contrast or sprezzature-colors-cvd .

### Does sprezzature-colors check the colours of my web page?

No: sprezzature-colors audits the colour pairs of a palette (a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, a text format in which programs store data as named fields, like {"name": "Ada"}) file whose keys start with label- , brand- or surface- ), and simulates colour blindness on an image such as a screenshot; it does not read HTML or CSS (Cascading Style Sheets, the rules that give a web page its colours, fonts and spacing). Contrast on a rendered page against its real background is the job of a browser-based tool such as axe-core or Lighthouse.

### How is sprezzature-colors different from an online contrast checker?

sprezzature-colors checks at once every pair of a palette that can appear together in a theme ( --all-pairs for the full cross-product), at the ratio set with --target , where an online checker tests one foreground and background typed by hand. For each failure it suggests the nearest passing colour with the same hue and saturation, only lighter or darker, and it runs offline, from a script or a CI (continuous integration, the server that re-runs a project's checks on every change and turns red when one fails) job.

### Does sprezzature-colors send my files to a cloud service or use AI?

No: sprezzature-colors is deterministic colour arithmetic that calls no AI model and never touches the network, so it needs no Ollama; and the simulation writes its images on your own disk, next to the source by default.

### Can I run sprezzature-colors in CI?

Yes: sprezzature-colors-contrast --palette palette.json exits 0 when every pair passes, 1 when one fails and 2 when the palette yields no pair to check, and --format json gives a report a CI job can parse. An HTTP API ( POST /v1/contrast ) runs the same check for a pipeline written in another language.

### Can I use sprezzature-colors without Claude Code?

Yes: sprezzature-colors is a Python library ( import sprezzature_colors as sc ), a command line, an HTTP API with a Docker image, and an MCP server, sprezzature-colors-mcp , for any MCP client. The Docker image runs that server, so one port answers both the HTTP routes and /mcp .

### Is sprezzature-colors free?

Yes: sprezzature-colors is open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account, API key or paid tier, and the source is on GitHub .

# Figures — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/figures.html

sprezzature-figures

# Figures

## How to get a figure

Ask our tool in plain words, from a sankey to a SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations, a chart of how much each input pushed one prediction up or down) plot:

"make a figure"

"chart this"

"treemap"

"candlestick"

"heatmap"

"sankey"

"SHAP plot"

"render this diagram"

Every figure below carries a kit: a zip with the data as a CSV (comma-separated values, a table saved as plain text, one row per line with the cells separated by commas — what a spreadsheet exports), the generator that reads it, and the interactive SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, a picture stored as drawing instructions rather than pixels, so it stays sharp at any zoom) it writes. Two Python files, no build step, and for most of them nothing to install at all. The five glyph maps sit on the maps page and the two animated Gapminder generators on the Hans ROSLING tribute ; with the 160 below, that is the whole 168-kind catalogue.

FIGURES.md catalog
⭐ on GitHub

## Time series & trends

How a value moves over an ordered axis: lines, areas and event timelines, down to the ACF (autocorrelation function, how closely a series matches itself shifted back in time) and OHLC (open, high, low, close: a trading day's four prices in one bar) charts.

Sparklines : Twenty metrics, one screen.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (59 KB)

Small multiples : One panel each, one scale for all.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (60 KB)

Line chart : A value over an ordered axis, one line per series.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (56 KB)

Multi-line : Two series over time with points.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (56 KB)

Area chart : How a whole made of categories evolves over time.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (54 KB)

Stacked area : Composition of series over time.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (52 KB)

Step / stairs : A value that changes at discrete points.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (51 KB)

↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (65 KB)

Streamgraph : Stacked areas on a wiggle baseline over time.
↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (67 KB)

↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (77 KB)

↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (64 KB)

↓ Python + CSV + SVG kit (61 KB)

SHAP beeswarm : Every row's explanation, and when the colour lies.

Partial dependence and ICE (individual conditional expectation, one line per row showing how its prediction moves as one input changes): The average effect, and the rows that disagree with it.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-figures?

Run pip install sprezzature-figures (Python 3.10 to 3.13): one command installs the generators, the command line, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server and the editor, with no extras to choose. It is free and open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, and sprezzature-figures render bar --out check.svg checks the install.

### How many chart types does sprezzature-figures have?

sprezzature-figures has +150 chart types in its catalogue, all marked stable, and sprezzature-figures list prints them. The gallery on this page shows all but seven of them on purpose: the five glyph maps are on the maps page and the two animated Gapminder figures on the Hans ROSLING page .

### Which file formats can sprezzature-figures export?

sprezzature-figures writes SVG by default, self-contained with its fonts embedded, and the --out extension also picks .png , .jpg , .pdf or .html . PNG, JPEG and PDF are rasterised from that SVG inside Python, and --scale 3 upsamples them for high-density screens.

### What is the Ralph Eyeball Loop?

The Ralph Eyeball Loop is how sprezzature-figures looks at a figure before calling it done: it renders an SVG, an HTML page or a TikZ source to PNG, writes an assessment, and you edit the source and run it again. By default the agent running it reads the picture; with --local , the vision model qwen3-vl:8b served by Ollama writes the critique offline. It is the script scripts/ralph_eyeball_loop.py in the repository, explained on its own page .

### Does sprezzature-figures send my data to a cloud service?

No: sprezzature-figures renders, recommends and checks figures on your machine with no model and no account. The three steps that use a model ( redraw , the editor chat and the eyeball loop's --local mode) call one served by Ollama locally by default, through best-engine-ai-helper. Used as a skill, the agent itself follows its own provider's data policy.

### What does sprezzature-figures need besides pip?

sprezzature-figures needs nothing more to render and check figures: the rasteriser and the fonts come with the package. redraw , which rebuilds a chart from a screenshot without inventing its numbers, and the editor chat need a model served by Ollama . The Ralph Eyeball Loop also uses system renderers (Chrome for HTML, tectonic for TikZ, rsvg-convert), and --check-tools lists which ones you have.

### Can I use sprezzature-figures without Claude Code, for example in CI?

Yes: sprezzature-figures is also a Python library ( make_figure ), a command line, an HTTP API with a Docker image, and the MCP server sprezzature-figures-mcp for any MCP client; the Claude Code skill is one of five ways in. In CI, sprezzature-figures check figure.svg exits 1 on any finding (labels printed over each other, text off the canvas, a dropped title), and --format json prints them for a program.

### How is sprezzature-figures different from matplotlib, Plotly or Vega-Lite?

matplotlib, Plotly and Vega-Lite give you an API or a grammar to compose a chart; sprezzature-figures gives you +150 finished chart kinds by name, each writing its SVG directly with no charting library underneath, and a checker that reads the result. For a live dashboard, a very large table or matplotlib's twenty years of answered questions, those tools remain the better choice, as LANDSCAPE.md in the repository says.

---

# Eleven short films — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/films.html

# Eleven short films

One on the suite, and one for each of its ten packages, from UI (user interface, the screens, buttons and forms a person works with) to turning a CLI (command-line interface, a tool driven by typing commands in a terminal) into a GUI (graphical user interface, a form with boxes to tick and a button to click). Nothing in them is a mock-up: the figures are the shipped SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, pictures stored as drawing instructions, sharp at any zoom) files, the maps are drawn on a real projection, the form was generated from the command that is installed, and the colour vision simulations came out of sprezzature-colors .

the whole suite

## Sprezzature 75 s

Design is know-how, and most of it is already written down: thirty laws of UX (user experience, how using a product feels: whether people find the button or give up), contrast ratios, a 2009 paper on colour vision, a projection from 2018. The suite is what happens when you point that know-how both ways — at making a thing, and at auditing it.

Landscape 3840×2160 Portrait 2160×3840 Square 2160×2160

Your browser cannot play this video.
Download the MP4 .

What it shows: six real outputs of the suite, the same rules used to make and to audit, and the Ralph Eyeball Loop on a shipped figure.

sprezzature-ui

## UI 75 s

The smallest brick, on purpose. Its job is the aesthetic judgement written in prose — the three-Roboto rule, the design tokens, what an interface has to respect — plus the one part of that judgement a machine can carry out.

Landscape 3840×2160 Portrait 2160×3840 Square 2160×2160

Your browser cannot play this video.
Download the MP4 .

What it shows: one sign-in screen in English, French and German under a layout that does not move, then the same panel in light and dark with a visible focus.

sprezzature-cli-gui

## CLI → GUI 75 s

A tool nobody will type, wrapped in a page. It does not read the help text — it reads the parser object, through argparse, Click or Typer, and falls back to running --help only when there is no parser to reach.

A document, becoming a site. Nine tools: a linter that runs on the standard library in milliseconds, favicons from one logo, the indexes a crawler and a language model both want, and readalong, which binds the narration to the page.

sprezzature-accessibility

## Accessibility 75 s

An unmuted autoplay masks a screen reader, and the markup says so on its own. Twenty rules from WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international rulebook that says, for example, how dark text must be against its background), each naming the element, the line and the rule it broke; six of them repair themselves, where there is exactly one safe repair.

Download the MP4 .

What it shows: a portrait a screen reader can only call “image”, then the description a local model drafts from the image and the page around it.

sprezzature-colors

## Colors 75 s

Light grey on white reads fine — to you, indoors. About one man in twelve sees red and green as the same bar, and no amount of care changes that, because the information is not in their eye.

Landscape 3840×2160 Portrait 2160×3840 Square 2160×2160

Your browser cannot play this video.
Download the MP4 .

What it shows: a pastel booking card erased by sunlight, the colour fix that keeps its blue and its grey, and one chart seen by four kinds of eyes.

sprezzature-audio

## Audio 75 s

One modality, read in both directions. Captions turn sound into timed text; narration turns text into timed sound, landing as a WAV (Waveform Audio File Format, uncompressed sound, the file a voice recorder saves) plus a WebVTT — exactly like a transcript does, which is what lets a page follow the reading sentence by sentence.

Download the MP4 .

What it shows: the same words captioned twice, as one line flashing by and as two lines with time to read, and the two directions of the package.

sprezzature-ux-laws

## Laws of UX 75 s

Nobody says “that violates Hick’s Law”. They say the page is overwhelming, or that they can never find the button. Thirty laws, curated by Jon YABLONSKI; eight of them a machine can decide from the markup alone.

## Figures 75 s

+150 kinds of chart across 52 categories, every one hand-authored. No charting library sits underneath any of it: each generator writes the SVG markup itself, and the vector is the deliverable rather than an export.

A column of countries is a map waiting to happen. Real coastlines, a real projection, eight kilometres of relief — and a choice about which distortion you are willing to accept, stated rather than defaulted to.

sprezzature-video

## Video 75 s

The brick that made the other ten films, and the one that checks them. A film is a claim with a soundtrack: every number on screen is verified against the code that produces it, including the numbers nobody declared.

Landscape 3840×2160 Portrait 2160×3840 Square 2160×2160

Your browser cannot play this video.
Download the MP4 .

What it shows: the number this suite once got wrong on screen, caught and corrected against the code.

## About these films

Each film exists twice, and the two do not mix: an English film is English throughout — on screen, in the voice, in the subtitles — and a French film is French throughout. This page serves the English cut; the French one is a click away.

The voices come from the suite itself: sprezzature-audio through Kokoro, with a pronunciation lexicon so that WebVTT, RTTM (Rich Transcription Time Marked, a text file listing who speaks from which second to which), OKLCH (OK Lightness, Chroma, Hue, a colour written as how light, how vivid and which hue) and GMTED2010 (Global Multi-resolution Terrain Elevation Data 2010, the height of the ground worldwide) are said the same way in every film and in both languages. The same call writes the subtitles, off the same timeline as the audio.

Each film is cut three ways and all three are on this page: wide for a screen, tall for a phone held upright, square for a feed. Pick one above the player. The three are frame-synced, so the same sentence lands on the same second whichever you watch; only the layout moves. All of them are 4K.

They follow Guy KAWASAKI’s order, which is why the rail above each frame says where you are: what the thing is, then the problem, then what the package does about it, then the secret sauce (the part you would not guess, with the sources it rests on, named so you can go and check them), then the finest thing the package can show, and then your turn. The first frame is already a finished one: the name, one sentence, and where to find it. The last is the only ask, and one line to keep.

They were built with the same discipline they describe. Every scene was rendered to a still and looked at before the film was encoded, which is how the sixty-second set that came before this one was caught quoting a catalogue size the package had outgrown months earlier, off a screenshot taken in September, naming a font the package does not ship, and counting twelve font files where there are six.

Two of those were typography rather than fact, and they now have a test instead of an eye: it measures every line of film text in the font the films are set in, and fails if one wraps and leaves its last word standing alone.

---

# Sprezzature — ten Claude / OpenCode skills for vanilla JS + Tailwind

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/

# Sprezzature

in the broadest sense
Create and audit figures, visualizations for app and web content,
faithful to a standard of accessibility, chromatic rigor, and usability.

Explore
the ten skills
See
the gallery
⭐ on GitHub

10 packages
+150 chart types
21 map plates
0 accounts needed

## One minute

What the suite does, and the one thing nothing
else does: it refuses to trust a figure it has not looked at. English throughout — on screen,
in the voice, in the subtitles.

Your browser cannot play this video.
Download the MP4 .

Ten
more films, one per package →

## Getting started

Sprezzature is a set of skills for
Claude Code or OpenCode . Install the ones you want, then ask in plain
language. The skill both makes the artifact and audits it.

*]:min-w-0">

### 1 · Install

Grab the latest release, copy the skills you
want into your runtime.

VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/warith-harchaoui/sprezzature/releases/latest \
| sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"v\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p') # the latest release, resolved
curl -L https://github.com/warith-harchaoui/sprezzature/releases/download/v${VERSION}/sprezzature-skills-${VERSION}.tar.gz | tar xz

mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills # OpenCode: ~/.opencode/skills
cp -r sprezzature-ui sprezzature-figures ~/.claude/skills/
Just want one tool, no agent? Each deterministic tool also ships as a standalone pip package. See Packages .

### 2 · Ask, in plain English

Trigger phrases route the request; the skill
makes it, then audits it against the rules.

"make this page accessible" → sprezzature-accessibility lints the HTML and reports what to fix.

"make a figure of this CSV" (comma-separated values, a table saved as plain text, one row per line with the cells separated by commas — what a spreadsheet exports) → sprezzature-figures draws it, then audits the chart.

"wrap this CLI in a GUI" (a CLI, command-line interface, is a tool you drive by typing commands; a GUI, graphical user interface, is a form you click) → sprezzature-cli-gui scaffolds a usable interface.

Full install options (checksums, OpenCode + local Ollama, upgrades) →

## The tool ecosystem

Each skill's scripts also ship as a standalone package, reachable five ways : a self-contained zip, a Python library, an API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) tools for an agent, or the skill itself. Same implementation behind all of them.

## The ten skills

## A taste of what it renders

A few frames from sprezzature-figures : our house style and images made with care, on a fitting palette. The full catalog of charts and statistical plots has its own page.

See
the full gallery →

## What's unusual

### Make and audit

Build from scratch or on an existing codebase, then
audit the result against the rules.

### The models can run on your machine

The text, audio and vision models could run locally if you ask for it; nothing has to leave the
machine.

### Opinionated graphical choices

Skills cover accessibility, colors, typography,
languages, search-engine optimization (SEO, coming up when someone searches Google), and generative-engine optimization (GEO, being cited by an AI assistant such as ChatGPT).

### Runtime-portable

Skills serve Claude Code and OpenCode or completely locally and free.

## Highlights

### 👁️ Look at the figure before you ship it

You can proofread a sentence by reading it back. You
can't do that with a chart: whether it's right lives in the pixels, not the code. So the Ralph
Eyeball Loop takes whatever you made (an SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, a picture stored as drawing instructions rather than pixels, so it stays sharp at any zoom) figure, a TikZ figure, a whole web
page) and renders it to an image with a deterministic tool, no model involved. Then something actually looks
at it: by default the agent itself, the same one that wrote the code, or, fully offline, an optional local
vision model. It catches what a code check never will: a label cut off at the edge, a legend that slid off
the canvas, two nodes sitting on top of each other, colors that vanish for a colorblind reader. Fix the
source, render again, look again. It's a prescribed review loop, not an autonomous critic. Everyone else
aims this at web pages. We aim it at charts and diagrams too.

How the Ralph Eyeball Loop works →

### 📐 The figure is a real SVG, not a picture

A figure ships as carefully written scalable vector graphics
(SVG). The generators emit the markup directly, each with a matching viewBox , so the graphic scales to any size without a blurry pixel and the
text stays selectable. The generator writes SVG directly, so there is no separate chart-description spec to
export, and the Portable Network Graphics (PNG) is only an export for
places that can't take vector art. The SVG is the deliverable.

## State of the Art

The full landscape (15 category matrices) lives in
LANDSCAPE.md
( français ).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is sprezzature?

sprezzature is a suite of ten open-source Python packages, each also an agent skill for Claude Code and OpenCode, that make and then audit the craft around code: interfaces, figures, maps, colours, accessibility, captions, narration, publishing, the laws of UX and the claims a film makes. Every artifact a tool makes is checked against explicit rules before it ships.

### How do I install sprezzature?

Run pip install sprezzature (Python 3.10 to 3.13): it installs all ten packages, with no extras to choose. Then sprezzature-skills --install copies the skills into ~/.claude/skills , or sprezzature-skills --install --agent opencode for OpenCode.

### Do I need Claude Code or an AI agent to use it?

No: every sprezzature package also works on its own as a Python library, a command line, an HTTP API with a Docker image, and an MCP server for any MCP client; the agent skill is one of five ways in. Each package has its own pip install , listed on the packages page .

### Is sprezzature free?

Yes. Every package is open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account, API key or paid tier, and the source is on GitHub .

### Does my data leave my machine?

Not unless you send it somewhere: sprezzature's tools run locally. The ones that use a model (alt text, plain-language rewrites, translation, the local eyeball check) call a model served by Ollama on your own machine, transcription runs whisper.cpp locally, and the voices are synthesised locally. When you use them as skills, the agent itself follows its own provider's data policy.

### What does “make and audit” mean?

Each sprezzature package both produces something (a page, a chart, a map, a caption track, a narration) and audits it, or audits what you already have, against written rules, with a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, a text format in which programs store data as named fields, like {"name": "Ada"}) report and an exit code a CI (continuous integration, the server that re-runs a project's checks on every change and turns red when one fails) job can fail on. Most audits can also apply the repairs they are sure of with --fix .

### Which AI agents does it work with?

The sprezzature skills are written for Claude Code and OpenCode, and every package also runs an MCP server (for example sprezzature-figures-mcp ), so any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol can call the same tools.

### How do I report a problem or contribute?

Report a sprezzature problem or propose a change by opening an issue or a pull request on GitHub ; each package lives in its own repository, linked from its page on this site. A star on the repository helps others find the suite.

# Maps — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/maps.html

sprezzature · case studies

# Maps

Publication-grade plates for any region on Earth: real elevation, real borders, and a configuration file you can argue with, written in YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language, a plain-text settings format of indented lines like region: Sahel). Conflict events come from ACLED (the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project, which logs each reported battle, protest or attack with its date and place) and UCDP (the Uppsala Conflict Data Program, the Swedish university record of armed conflicts since 1946).

Work in progress: the generators are versioned and every map below is rebuilt from them in one command, but the cartographic judgement is still being revised plate by plate — label placement, relief strength and the confidence scale have all changed this month. Read these as illustrations of the method, not as operational assessments.

← All case studies

## The plates

A layered reference plate for any region: coastline, international frontiers, country labels, a bathymetry contour halo, dual-unit scale bar and north arrow, on an auto-centred Lambert Conformal Conic projection (conformal, so shapes and angles stay true at city/province scale). Borders switch automatically between Natural Earth's 50m and 10m tiers depending on how zoomed in the region is. Put thematic layers on top of that plate and it becomes a geopolitics-desk product: classed pastel fills with white boundary casing, letter-spaced place labels, flashpoint markers, tapered axes of advance, and a floating legend.

Every areas-of-control plate below is schematic, says so on its own face, and keeps its claim lines in readable Python rather than an opaque data file: a reader who disagrees can see exactly which coordinates to argue with. None of it is intelligence. The reference and chokepoint plates assert nothing beyond Natural Earth's own geography.

Region
All Europe Africa Middle East Asia-Pacific Americas

Shows
All Reference geography Areas of control Chokepoints & sea lanes

↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (247 KB)

↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (177 KB)

↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (385 KB)

The Dnieper Line : the plate that goes with an article: four numbered notes, placed automatically clear of every name, around the stretch where a river became the front.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (327 KB)

↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (351 KB)

Syria : a four-way split, an illustrative snapshot from around 2018.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (355 KB)

Israel and Palestine, 1949 : the armistice lines as they stood until June 1967. The 1947 partition plan is named, not drawn: no open vector of it exists.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (418 KB)

June 1967 : six days, four territories, as the difference between two dated records. Named as the UN names them: occupied.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (369 KB)

1967 to 2005 : what was handed back and what was kept: Sinai in 1982, Gaza in 2005, the West Bank and the Golan still held.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (364 KB)

Today : the Oslo areas, the settlements, and Gaza behind a yellow line, from the March–April 2026 layers of OCHA (the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, which maps checkpoints and access for aid workers).
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (651 KB)

Libya : loyalist, rebel and the contested oil crescent, around spring 2011.
↓ YAML + Python + PNG kit (321 KB)

No plate matches both filters yet. Clearing one of them brings the rest back.

Every plate here is generated by sprezzature-maps , from the builders in scripts/build_situation_examples.py . The configuration behind each one is the kit on its card.

## Thematic maps

Further glyph and cartogram techniques from sprezzature-figures, layered over the same offline Natural Earth basemap.

Proportional-symbol map : Area-true √-scaled bubbles on a world basemap.

Connection / flow map : Great-circle arcs weighted by volume.

Pie-glyph map : A small pie chart placed at each region.

Bar-glyph map : Mini bar charts placed at each region.

Tile-grid cartogram : One equal tile per country, geographic layout.

Small multiples : One panel per year, class breaks frozen.

## For conflict research: ACLED and UCDP, at the precision they record

The two datasets peace-and-conflict research runs on — ACLED and the UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset — each record, beside every coordinate, how well that coordinate is known . ACLED codes geo_precision 1–3; UCDP codes where_prec 1–7. Those are not file metadata: ACLED’s 3 is a provincial capital standing in for a whole province, and UCDP’s 6 means only the country is known and the coordinates are a representative point for an entire state.

Maps of this data draw all of them as the same dot. That asserts a street corner the source never gave, once per row, several hundred times a figure. Here the code reaches the mark:

A named location
A solid disc with a white casing. The mark means what it has always meant: we know the place.

A place standing in for an area
A hollow ring. The old cartographic signal for “about here”, and unlike a disc of invented radius it claims nothing it cannot support. Where the dataset states a radius — UCDP’s where_prec 2 says about 25 km — it is drawn, to the plate’s own scale.

A region pinned to its capital
A hollow broken ring: one step further from “a place”. The date is spoken the same way, from time_precision — “week of”, “month of”, “in 2023”.

Rows that cannot be placed honestly are not placed . A UCDP where_prec 6 row is refused a dot by default, and the count goes onto the plate’s own method line rather than disappearing — a silent drop being the other half of the same dishonesty.

The step between the file and the mark is one call. acled_events("sudan-2024.csv", derive_region=True) returns a config fragment whose every key the generator already read, so cfg.update(...) is the whole integration and a hand-written config keeps everything it says. ucdp_events does the same for the GED (Georeferenced Event Dataset, one row per deadly event with its date and coordinates).

Column names, code ranges and the wording of each code are taken from the ACLED codebook and the UCDP GED codebook, read rather than recalled. What this package deliberately leaves to CShapes, PRIO-GRID (the Peace Research Institute Oslo grid, which cuts the world into half-degree squares for conflict statistics), geoBoundaries and GeoPandas is listed in LANDSCAPE.md .

## How the situation maps are built

Every map above is a hand-authored SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, a picture stored as drawing instructions rather than pixels, so it stays sharp at any zoom) document: no chart-grammar library, no headless browser, no external tiles fetched at render time. Everything geographic is a vendored, offline Natural Earth asset.

Natural Earth, 50m and 10m
Public-domain vector borders, vendored offline. Situation maps pick the tier automatically from how zoomed-in the requested region is.

Real elevation, not a flat hillshade
Situation maps compute their relief from real GMTED2010 (Global Multi-resolution Terrain Elevation Data 2010, the US Geological Survey's map of ground height worldwide) elevation: a directional hillshade blended with texture shading (Brown, 2010: a fractional-order Laplacian applied in the frequency domain), which draws out ridgelines and drainage networks at every scale at once, then retinted warm-highlight/cool-shadow instead of flat grey. Reprojected pixel by pixel into each map's own Lambert Conformal Conic projection, through its exact analytic inverse.

Millimetres, not pixels
Nature wants 90 mm for a single column, Science 57. Ask for one and the file lands at that size in a layout instead of at whatever a consumer infers — and the plate measures its own smallest label against that width and tells you what it will really be. Dropped into a 90 mm column, a label can set at 1.6 pt and render without complaint, because a vector file always does.

PDF and EPS (Encapsulated PostScript, the vector file print shops ask for) come out drawn, not photographed
A raster inside a PDF wrapper satisfies the extension and nothing a journal wants, and nobody can tell until they zoom in. Vector export goes through rsvg-convert — an optional system package. Without it the page is still written at the right physical size, with a warning saying it is a raster and what to install.

## Real data: the last five French presidential runoffs

The same carefully authored SVG map engine, on real data from the French Ministère de l'Intérieur: the winner's second-round vote share by département across the last five presidential elections, on one frozen blue scale so the panels compare. 2002 (the republican sprezzature against the far right) is near-uniform; 2012 (the closest) is the palest; 2017 and 2022 show the lighter départements where Marine Le Pen ran strongest.

Real data: the last five French presidential runoffs

Year
Winner
%
Runner-up
%

2002 Jacques Chirac 82.21 Jean-Marie Le Pen 17.79

2007 Nicolas Sarkozy 53.06 Ségolène Royal 46.94

2012 François Hollande 51.64 Nicolas Sarkozy 48.36

2017 Emmanuel Macron 66.10 Marine Le Pen 33.90

2022 Emmanuel Macron 58.55 Marine Le Pen 41.45

Source: Ministère de l'Intérieur (2nd-round results by département).

## Map techniques (carefully authored SVG)

When a projection or a glyph falls outside a chart grammar, the same loop drives a carefully drawn Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) map instead.

Dot-density map : One dot per N people inside real regions.

Hexbin map : Hexagonal binning of point density over a map.

Spike map : Vertical spikes at locations, height by value.

Hexbin map : Earthquakes binned into hexagons by count, tracing the Ring of Fire.

Binned grid map : Square-bin aggregation over geography, cells coloured by count.

×

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-maps?

Run pip install sprezzature-maps (Python 3.10 to 3.13): one command installs the three generators, the make-map command line, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server and the editor, and pulls in sprezzature-figures, whose font and rendering code it shares. It is free and open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence.

### What kinds of maps can sprezzature-maps draw?

sprezzature-maps draws its plates as SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, the vector image format browsers read): a situation_map that centres itself on any region with a Lambert conformal conic projection and layers zones, events and a two-unit scale bar, and a density map of where point events fell. make-map situation-new --country Moldova writes a starter configuration for a new regional plate.

### Where does sprezzature-maps get its map data?

sprezzature-maps ships its geography inside the package: Natural Earth borders, coastlines, lakes and rivers, elevation from GMTED2010 (the Global Multi-resolution Terrain Elevation Data of 2010, from the US Geological Survey) for the relief, and administrative units for the United States, France, Germany, Italy and Switzerland. Your own numbers come as rows of CSV (comma-separated values, a table saved as plain text, one row per line, what a spreadsheet exports) or TSV (the same, with tabs) or JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), and acled_events and ucdp_events turn an export from ACLED (the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project) or from UCDP (the Uppsala Conflict Data Program) into a situation-map layer.

### Does sprezzature-maps work offline?

Yes: sprezzature-maps needs no tile server, no API key and no account, because the base maps and the elevation are bundled, and the finished SVG carries its own fonts. The only steps that use a model are make-map improve and the editor's repair loop, which call a vision model served by Ollama on your machine by default.

### What does sprezzature-maps need besides pip?

sprezzature-maps needs nothing more to render SVG, PNG or JPEG. A vector PDF or EPS uses the system tool rsvg-convert (librsvg); without it, the package writes a raster page and says so. make-map improve needs a local vision model, reached through best-engine-ai-helper and Ollama .

### Can I use sprezzature-maps without Claude Code, for example in CI (continuous integration, the server that re-runs a project's checks on every change)?

Yes: sprezzature-maps is also a Python library, a command line ( make-map or sprezzature-maps ), an HTTP API with a Docker image, and the MCP server sprezzature-maps-mcp ; the Claude Code skill is one of five ways in. In CI, make-map audit reads finished plates against eleven rules (a named classification, printed breaks, a stated date, a title) and exits 1 on any finding, with --format json for a program.

### How is sprezzature-maps different from Folium, kepler.gl or QGIS (the free desktop mapping program, its name short for Quantum Geographic Information System)?

Folium and kepler.gl make maps a reader pans and zooms over tiles or a GPU (graphics processing unit, the chip that draws a screen) layer, and QGIS is a desktop GIS (geographic information system, software that stores, joins and measures places on a map) for analysing geography; sprezzature-maps draws one static, publication-ready plate as a self-contained SVG, and an audit that reads it back. If the geography still needs joining or buffering, or the map has to move, those tools are the better choice, as LANDSCAPE.md in the repository says.

# Packages — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/packages.html

standalone packages

# Packages

Every tool here is one implementation reached six different ways. Which one you want depends on what you are doing: sending a colleague a single file, importing a function, typing a command, calling it from another language, handing it to an agent, or letting Claude read the skill. None of those should require a different tool.

Each package carries the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, is local-first, and is independently versioned. All ten are published on PyPI, so a plain pip install is enough.

## Six ways in

The rule is that these are surfaces , never re-implementations. A route, a tool description and a command line all call the same function; when they disagree, one of them is a bug rather than a variant. Five of these six are the contract every package holds — library, command line or CLI (command-line interface, a tool you drive by typing commands in a terminal), an API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), agent tools over MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English), skill. The zip kit is a way of delivering one, not a sixth implementation.

zip

### A single self-contained kit

One folder that runs on a machine with nothing installed: the generator, the drawing engine in one file, the data, a page that opens the result, and a README. No network, no clone, no account. This is the form you can attach to an email.

library

### Python functions

Import them and call them. Typed, documented, and free of any plotting or charting dependency: the SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, a picture stored as drawing instructions rather than pixels, so it stays sharp at any zoom) is written directly, so the only thing you install is the thing you asked for.

cli

### Two command lines over one engine

Every package ships an argparse front door and a Click twin — make-a11y and sprezzature-accessibility , make-colors and sprezzature-colors , and so on. argparse because it is in the standard library and therefore always there; Click because the people using it expect it. Where a package has several tools the two doors read one catalogue, so neither can offer a command the other is missing. Where Click is not already needed it is an optional extra and the import is guarded: a package whose audit runs on the standard library alone stays that way.

api

### HTTP, via FastAPI

The same functions over HTTP, so any language that can make a request can use them. Comes with OpenAPI docs at /docs , which is also how the argument names stay honest: they are generated from the signatures, not written by hand.

mcp

### Agent tools, via FastAPI MCP

The HTTP routes republished as Model Context Protocol tools, so an assistant calls them as first-class tools rather than by guessing at a shell command. Deliberately a wrapper over the existing routes: a hand-written MCP server would be a second copy of the surface, free to drift from it.

skills

### Skills, for Claude and for OpenCode

The judgement that is not in the code: when to reach for a chart type, what makes a title honest, which check to run before shipping. MCP gives an agent the ability ; a skill gives it the taste . Both runtimes read the same source material.

## Where each surface actually exists

Five surfaces is the contract, and all ten packages hold it. Every one has an HTTP API and an MCP surface over its library: the same functions, never a second copy. The zip is the sixth door and is not owed by the contract — five packages ship a toolbox kit (accessibility, cli-gui, colors, maps, ux-laws), figures ships one per figure instead (160 of them) and maps twelve plates besides its own; audio, publish and ui have none yet. The skills need no second version for OpenCode: both runtimes read the same SKILL.md .

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I have to install all ten sprezzature packages?

No: each sprezzature package installs on its own, for example pip install sprezzature-colors , with no extra to choose. pip install sprezzature is the shortcut that installs all ten at once, plus the sprezzature-skills command.

### How do I install the sprezzature skills for my agent?

Install the sprezzature hub with pip install sprezzature , then run sprezzature-skills --install to copy the skills into ~/.claude/skills for Claude Code, or sprezzature-skills --install --agent opencode for OpenCode.

### How do I update sprezzature?

Update every sprezzature package at once with pip install --upgrade sprezzature , then run sprezzature-skills --install again so the copies your agent reads match the installed packages.

### Can I call a sprezzature package from an agent that is not Claude Code?

Yes: every sprezzature package ships an MCP server, such as sprezzature-figures-mcp , so any client that speaks the Model Context Protocol can call its tools. Each package also has a Python library, a command line and an HTTP API with a Docker image.

### Where is the source code of each sprezzature package?

Each sprezzature package has its own repository on GitHub , linked from its row in the table on this page, under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence.

# Publishing — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/publish.html

sprezzature-publish

# Publishing

Turn a folder of Markdown into a static site: per-page meta tags, a full favicon / progressive web app (PWA, a website a phone can install like an app)-icon set from one logo, robots + sitemap + llms.txt + feeds, plain-language rewrites, and local text-to-speech (TTS) narration.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

Per-page Open Graph + Twitter Card + Schema.org JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, data written as named fields, like {"name": "Ada"}) for Linking Data (JSON-LD, the hidden block that tells a search engine who wrote the page and what it is about)

A full favicon / app-icon / PWA-icon set from one logo, plus a webmanifest

robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, Atom / Really Simple Syndication (RSS, a feed that tells a news-reader app each time a page appears), humans.txt

Plain-language rewrites and audio (MP3) narration via local open-source (OSS, code anyone may read and reuse) TTS

A read-along bound to that narration, highlighting the sentence being spoken — and it applies to an existing HTML page with no Markdown behind it

## Audits

Lint Markdown and catch broken links before publishing

Readability / grade-level checks on the copy

The audio and the page leave the same Markdown by different roads, so the two sentence lists are compared and the first divergence raises. A read-along one sentence out of step is worse than none: it points at the wrong line, with confidence

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I install sprezzature-publish?

Run pip install sprezzature-publish on Python 3.10 to 3.13: that one line installs all thirteen tools, the API (Application Programming Interface, web addresses another program sends a request to and gets an answer from) served over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol, the way a browser asks a server for a page), and the MCP (Model Context Protocol, the protocol through which AI agents call tools in English) server, with no extras to choose. sprezzature-publish is free and open source under the BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, a University of California licence that lets anyone use, change or sell the code as long as the copyright notice stays) 3-Clause licence, with no account or API key.

### What does sprezzature-publish need besides pip?

sprezzature-publish needs Ollama running on your machine only for the tools that ask a local model: sprezzature-publish-meta , sprezzature-publish-plain , sprezzature-publish-faq (unless --no-llm ), sprezzature-publish-lint --ai and sprezzature-publish-narrate --ai-hints . Linting, rendering, icons, indexes, audits and the call-to-action check need no model. Narration needs its voice files once, fetched with sprezzature-audio-install-voice --engine kokoro .

### Does sprezzature-publish send my content to a cloud service?

No: sprezzature-publish runs locally. Meta tags, plain-language rewrites and FAQ answers are drafted by a model served by Ollama on your own machine, and narration is synthesised by a local open-source text-to-speech engine. Auditing a live URL reads that page and never writes to it.

### Does sprezzature-publish handle SEO (search engine optimisation, being found on Google), GEO (generative engine optimisation, being cited by ChatGPT), AEO (answer engine optimisation, being the quoted answer) and llms.txt?

Yes: sprezzature-publish covers all four, and sprezzature-publish-findable writes one report for search, generative and answer engines (SEO, GEO, AEO), money pages first, with --fix for the deterministic repairs. sprezzature-publish-indexes writes robots.txt , sitemap.xml , llms.txt , llms-full.txt , an Atom or RSS feed and humans.txt , and its --offer and --cta options put what the site is for at the top of llms.txt .

### Can sprezzature-publish write an FAQ with FAQPage JSON-LD?

Yes: sprezzature-publish drafts the FAQ a site is missing with sprezzature-publish-faq , from the site's own pages, ranking the questions by the calls to action declared in ctas.yaml and listing apart the ones the site cannot answer yet. sprezzature-publish-faq site/ --audit --fix rebuilds the FAQPage JSON-LD from the visible FAQ, and the tool never claims that markup makes a page rank.

### Can sprezzature-publish narrate a blog post?

Yes: sprezzature-publish reads a Markdown post, or an HTML page with --scope , aloud with a local voice through sprezzature-publish-narrate , and writes the timed track beside the WAV (Waveform Audio File Format, uncompressed sound, the file a recorder saves) or MP3. sprezzature-publish-readalong then binds it to the page so the sentence being spoken is highlighted, and its --check catches a page edited after the recording. The voices come from sprezzature-audio , installed with it.

### How is sprezzature-publish different from MkDocs, Hugo, Jekyll or Yoast?

sprezzature-publish is sized for a README, a docs/ folder and a blog: for a hundred versioned pages or a team, MkDocs Material, Hugo or Astro are the better choice, as its own README says. Unlike an SEO plugin such as Yoast, which works inside one CMS (content management system, the back office such as WordPress where a site is edited), it builds pages and can also audit and repair the head of a site it did not build. It adds an icon set from one logo, llms.txt , a grounded FAQ and a narrated read-along.

### Can I run sprezzature-publish in CI, without Claude Code?

Yes: sprezzature-publish works without any agent, as a Python library, a command line, an HTTP API with a Docker image that runs sprezzature-publish-mcp , and an MCP server. In CI, sprezzature-publish-lint exits 1 on any error with only click and the standard library behind it, and sprezzature-publish-audit and sprezzature-publish-findable exit 1 on an error finding, with --format json for a machine to read.

# The Ralph Eyeball Loop — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/ralph-eyeball-loop.html

👁️ the idea

# The Ralph Eyeball Loop

You can proofread a sentence by reading it back. You can't do that with a chart. So look at the chart, fix what your eye caught, and look again.

Render, look, critique, edit, then round again. Click to enlarge.

In Sprezzature , an AI agent runs this loop itself, refusing to trust a figure it hasn't looked at.

## Whether it's right lives in the pixels

Code that draws a chart can be correct and the chart still be wrong. A label slides off the edge. A legend lands on top of the data. Two points sit exactly on each other. A red-and-green palette turns into one muddy colour for a reader who can't tell them apart. None of that shows up when you read the source. It only shows up when you see the result.

Text is easy this way: you read it back and the mistake is right there. A picture is not. The only honest test of a picture is to look at it.

## The loop, in four steps

1 Render. Turn whatever you made (a chart, a diagram, a map, a whole web page) into a plain image with a deterministic tool. No model, no guessing. The same input gives the same picture every time.

2 Look. Actually study the image. Is the point you're making the first thing the eye finds? Is anything cut off, cramped, or on top of something else?

3 Fix the source. Change the spec, never the picture. The picture is only ever the evidence.

4 Do it again. Render, look, fix, until there is nothing left to catch. Then ship.

## Make, audit, then look

Three moves sit under everything in Sprezzature . You make the thing from code, so it reproduces exactly and carries its own data. You audit it with a static pass over the source that catches what the markup can already tell you: a rainbow scale, a blur filter, a missing title. Then you look , because whether it is actually right lives in the pixels.

Make proves it runs. Audit proves the source is clean. The Eyeball Loop proves the result reads. Each move catches what the other two let through, and together they turn "the file exported" into "the figure holds up." That is where the power is: a short, honest circuit you run until nothing is left to catch.

The loop reaches into accessibility too. Right after the render, a colour-vision simulator redraws the image the way a colour-blind reader sees it, and in plain grayscale. If a series or a plus-or-minus sign disappears once the colour is gone, that is a bug you fix before shipping, not a footnote.

## Eyes you don't have

This is the part worth dwelling on. A person with normal colour vision cannot see their own chart the way a colour-blind reader does, and no amount of care changes that, because the information is not in their eye. The simulator renders those other viewpoints, and the loop lets you look at them, so accessibility stops being a checklist you take on trust and becomes something you can see and correct. A review a person cannot physically perform turns into an ordinary step.

Grayscale is the sharpest single test. Total colour blindness is rare, but a figure that reads with no colour at all reads under every milder deficiency too. If the story survives grey, it survives everyone.

The palette also carries an accessibility level. The default is universal, already safe for colour vision, and high-contrast, monochrome, and per-deficiency variants are there on demand. One figure becomes a short ladder of renders, and the loop climbs it: render each level, simulate, look. You confirm the default reads for everyone, and that each stronger level does what it promises, with the same eyes in the same loop.

## Who does the looking?

By default, the agent that wrote the code does the looking, now checking its own output instead of trusting it. A small vision model can do the looking too if you ask for it.

Either way, the step that turns code into a picture is plain and deterministic. It holds no opinions. It's a prescribed review loop, not a black box that grades your work. You stay in charge; the loop just makes sure someone actually looked.

## Why we built the whole thing around it

Plenty of tools will screenshot a web page and check it. We point the same discipline at the harder stuff: charts, statistical plots, diagrams, and maps. These are the things people usually ship without ever looking, because the code ran and the file saved.

That habit is the difference between a figure that merely exports and one that actually reads. It is how every figure in the gallery reached print quality: we looked at the result and refused to ship until it held up.

See the gallery

# UI generation — Sprezzature

Source: https://sprezzature.ai/ui.html

sprezzature-ui

# user interface (UI) generation

Vanilla JavaScript (JS) + Tailwind UI: components, pages, forms, dialogs, dashboards, for teams shipping internal tools without a designer.

SKILL.md (the agent spec)
⭐ on GitHub

## Makes

Semantic HyperText Markup Language (HTML) + Tailwind: forms, modals, nav, dashboards, data tables, settings, empty states, skeletons

Dark-mode peers, focus rings, reduced-motion guards on by default

The three-Roboto type rule (sans + serif + mono), honoring any font you name

i18n (internationalisation, shortened to its first and last letters around the 18 between: every visible string kept apart, ready to translate) extracted to a single YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language, a plain-text settings file of indented lines like greeting: Hello) configuration shared by graphical user interface (GUI) and prompts — a model prompt is a translatable string, which almost nobody treats as one

## Audits

Audit existing UI against the stack + ergonomics rules

Audit i18n coverage and surface untranslated strings: translations embedded in JavaScript and HTML, prompts inlined in Python

The fix writes each string into the catalogue and stops there. It will not rewrite your call site — only you know whether that line wants a plural or a placeholder — so it prints the line to paste, and says which ones it could not parse with certainty
